newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends weaker on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends weaker on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The won ended weaker against the dollar on Wednesday as dealers covered for their short dollar positions on expectations the supply of dollars will remain tight this week, dealers said.
The won finished at 888.50 against Tuesday's close of 887.70. It opened at the day's high of 887.50 and fell to a monthly low of 888.60 shortly before the close.
A Korea First Bank dealer said the dollar supply had mostly dried up and few new supplies were expected this week.
Thursday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 887.70, unchanged from today.
The Korea First dealer said the won was likely to weaken further to 889 on Thursday.
A turnaround is expected next week when foreigners planning to invest in the local stock market would increase dollar liquidity, he added.
